chapter: Family, Margaret's story and Eutris's memories
title: Harlem in the mid-1930s: Lafayette Theatre and Chick Webb at the Savoy
summary: Mrs. H describes Sundays at the Lafayette Theatre and the Savoy where he played with Chick Webb.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: 1929-30, he was with Louis Russell. The year he went with Louis Armstrong - look, suppose we get it all -

I'll let him go through it and get all the dates. It's all back there somewhere, the date he went with Louis Armstrong, Fletcher Henderson. But I do know he came to New York. Chick Webb heard him, you know, and he went to play with Chick Webb, played the Savoy. I hadn't seen him for years and Edgar Hayes's wife and I was coming down Seventh Avenue. You know that was Harlem.
Could you tell us a little bit about it?
Harlem? There was nothing up here but integration with all the night clubs, everything. It was clean and it was beautiful, but I can't say it today.

That was back in '35, around '35, '36, before the War, before the Second World War. That's when we had the Lafayette Theatre. Every Sunday a whole gang of us would go to the Lafayette Theatre and then we'd leave there and go to Savoy because that's where he and all the gang were playing. They had two bands there every Sunday night.
Every Sunday night would it be a different band?
No, no, they played there regular.
He was playing with Chick Webb?
